skill.name: site-architecture
skill.description: Plans website page hierarchies, navigation systems, URL patterns, visual sitemaps, and internal linking strategies for new or restructured sites.
skill.summary: Design clear, search-friendly website structures with practical maps, navigation specifications, and linking plans.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Complex websites become difficult to navigate and maintain. This skill creates page hierarchies, URL maps, navigation specifications, visual sitemaps, and internal linking plans.
actual_capabilities: Gather business goals, audience needs, current site issues, page inventories, and URL constraints.
Recommend page hierarchies for SaaS, content, ecommerce, documentation, hybrid, and small business websites.
Produce ASCII hierarchies, Mermaid visual sitemaps, URL maps, and navigation specifications.
Define consistent URL patterns, breadcrumb structures, header navigation, footer navigation, and sidebar navigation.
Plan hub-and-spoke links, cross-section links, and orphan-page prevention.
limitations: Does not generate XML sitemaps or perform technical SEO audits.
Does not crawl live websites or verify analytics, rankings, redirects, or broken links.
Recommendations depend on the completeness of the supplied business context and page inventory.
Does not implement navigation components, redirects, schema markup, or content changes.

use_cases.title: Plan a SaaS Website
use_cases.description: Organize product, pricing, resource, integration, comparison, and company pages into a scalable structure.

use_cases.title: Restructure a Complex Site
use_cases.description: Group a large page inventory, reduce navigation complexity, and define clearer parent-child relationships.

use_cases.title: Scale Content Hubs
use_cases.description: Place articles, comparison pages, and integrations into hubs with consistent URLs and internal links.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Sitemap
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a site architecture for [business type]. Include essential pages, a simple hierarchy, recommended URLs, and primary navigation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a small or new website.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure a Growing Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Reorganize this page inventory: [pages]. Identify logical groups, propose parent-child relationships, preserve important URLs, and provide a redirect list.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an existing website has become difficult to navigate.

prompt_templates.title: Design Scalable Content Hubs
prompt_templates.prompt: Design architecture for [number] integration pages and [number] comparison pages. Define hubs, URL patterns, navigation placement, and internal linking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when adding large groups of repeatable pages.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this hierarchy and business context: [details]. Produce an improved ASCII tree, Mermaid sitemap, URL map, navigation specification, and linking plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a detailed redesign with multiple deliverables.

output_examples.input: Plan a website for an analytics platform with pricing, features, customer stories, documentation, and a blog.
output_examples.output: A three-level plan places Features, Pricing, Customers, Resources, and Company below the homepage. Analytics and reporting sit beneath Features.

output_examples.input: Reorganize a resource center containing articles, guides, webinars, templates, and case studies.
output_examples.output: A Resources hub groups each content type under a stable section. Related content links connect guides, templates, case studies, and product pages.

output_examples.input: Add 200 integration pages without placing every integration in the header.
output_examples.output: An Integrations hub supports individual integration pages with consistent paths. The header links only to the hub, while categories and cross-links improve discovery.

best_practices: Provide business goals, audience details, priority pages, and a complete page inventory.
Identify existing URLs that must remain stable or require redirects.
Review hierarchy, navigation, URLs, and internal links together before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not request an XML sitemap repair or technical crawl audit.
Do not omit legacy URLs when planning a website restructure.
Do not treat a generic template as final without adapting it to users and business goals.

faq.question: Can this skill plan both new and existing websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a new structure or reorganize an existing page inventory with redirect considerations.

faq.question: Does this skill create XML sitemaps?
faq.answer: No. It creates human-facing architecture plans and visual sitemaps, not technical XML sitemap files.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide site type, audiences, business goals, important pages, current URLs, planned sections, and known navigation problems.

faq.question: Can it produce a visual sitemap?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce Mermaid diagrams and ASCII trees that show page hierarchy and relationships.

faq.question: Will it implement redirects or navigation code?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend redirect mappings and navigation specifications, but implementation remains outside this skill.

faq.question: Does it include SEO guidance?
faq.answer: It covers search-friendly URLs, hierarchy, breadcrumbs, and internal links. It does not perform technical SEO diagnosis.
